_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: A permit halt is scoped by who asks for the permit. The audit it waits on is scoped by what stands in the grid queue, and the two do not reach the same projects.

introduction.text: The Governor [directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) to suspend action on all permits sought by data center projects](c1). The halt lasts until the grid operator finishes its audit. In the Governor's own words as CBS Texas carried them, [TCEQ will issue no permits sought by data center projects](c3) until data centers complete the ERCOT and water board audits.

The directive reaches past the one agency it is addressed to. The Texas Tribune reports that it says [no other state agency shall move forward with regulatory approvals related to data centers until this information is acquired](c2). One dated obligation follows from it, which is a [report to the Office of the Governor on its compliance with the directive](c4) by October 19th.

paragraphs.text: The halt is written around the applicant. It names permits sought by data center projects, which is a test a reviewer applies to whoever filed the paperwork. The audit it waits on is written around a process. The August letter aims it at [all data centers advancing through ERCOT's interconnection queue](c5). The Tribune's account of the September directive traces it to that same order, [ordering ERCOT on Aug. 3 to ensure data center developers provide information](c9).

The same directive says the agency [must align its permitting decisions with forthcoming audit results from ERCOT and the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB)](c11). That instruction is only as wide as the audits are. A project the audit never looks at produces nothing for a permit reviewer to align to.

The audit names one consequence and it is a grid consequence. [Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUCT and ERCOT, and by state law, must be denied connection to the Texas grid](c7). The Tribune reports the same consequence for a project that does not finish. [Projects that fail to complete the ERCOT audit are to be denied interconnection](c10). Refusal of a connection reaches a project that is asking for one.

sections.heading: The size of the queue is not the size of the gap

paragraphs.text: ERCOT is [currently tracking more than {{number:c8}} projects in the queue, representing over {{number:c8:1}} gigawatts of electricity](c8), the Texas Tribune reported on August 3rd. The Governor puts [approximately {{number:c23}} of the new power requests](c23) at data centers. Those are two different denominators, the whole queue and the new requests. Nothing in the record multiplies one by the other.
No published figure counts how many permits the halt reaches. None of the reports on the directive states a count, and this edition publishes none rather than an estimate dressed as a measurement.

A gas compression company says it will supply one data center with [{{number:c16}} megawatts of behind-the-meter, baseload power capacity](c16) from [approximately {{number:c17}} reciprocating natural gas-fueled generation units](c17). Deployment is [expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026](c18). Nothing in the record says whether that project sits in the queue the audit reads.

Being outside the queue is not the same as being outside the halt. The halt is scoped by who is asking for a permit. It never asks whether the project is in the queue, so the same directive reads one way by its first sentence and another way by its second.

sections.heading: What this edition does not establish

paragraphs.text: It does not establish that any behind-the-meter project needs, or escapes, an environmental permit. The agency publishes an [Overview of air permitting requirements and options for new internal combustion engine operations](c15). It also publishes a [List of facilities typically found at sources that need New Source Review permits](c14). Whether a particular installation needs one is a question this record does not answer, and no mechanism is asserted here.

It does not establish that any permit was refused, withdrawn or denied. What the record carries is a [canceled notice and comment hearing on data center permit O4791](c12). The agency says the hearing [will be rescheduled for a later date](c13) and gives no date.
